test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a term for the common local wind that blows in north and north-western parts of India during summers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Loo.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Loo** is a strong, dusty, gusty, hot, and dry summer wind from the west which blows over **the western Indo-Gangetic Plain region** of North India and Pakistan.
 
• It is particularly common in the months of May and June.
 
• The **Loo wind is known to cause severe heat waves** which can lead to heat strokes and other heat-related illnesses.
 
• People often take precautions such as staying indoors during peak hours and drinking plenty of fluids to avoid the adverse effects of the Loo.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bora**: A cold, northerly wind blowing from the Greek mountains to the Adriatic Sea.
 
• **Foehn**: A warm, dry wind descending the lee side of a mountain range, particularly in the Alps.
 
• **Chinook**: A warm, dry wind descending the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains in North America.
 
• These winds are different from the Loo as they occur in different regions and have different characteristics.
